The commit gate, the ledger and verify()

Source: vignettes/gate.Rmd
gate.Rmd

This article is for authors who keep a weft project in git. It follows one small report from its first commit to a release check. After it you will know what the commit gate refuses and how to answer it, what the ledger records and how changes() reads it, and how verify() checks a project before you hand it on.

The examples need git, Quarto and a project set up with use_weft(), so they are not run when this article is built. Each command was run in a scratch project, and the output shown is what it printed. Paths have been shortened.

Three checks, at three moments

weft checks a project at three moments:

When What runs What it reads
each commit the commit gate, gate() the static lints of the changed files, compared with HEAD
each render the checks in the document the values, the spans and the claims as they knit
before release verify() everything: lints, a full render, the ledgers

The commit gate is a commit-msg git hook that runs gate(). use_weft() installs it, or use_hooks() on its own. It compares what the commit will hold with HEAD, and refuses the commit for one of three reasons:

  1. a construct error in a changed document, whatever HEAD held;
  2. a tier-1 finding that HEAD did not hold, such as a newly typed number;
  3. weft constructs removed, when the commit message does not say so.

The gate runs no R code from the project and renders nothing. It reads git only, so it takes a fraction of a second.

A report before weft

The report starts as an ordinary Quarto document, committed to git:

---
title: "Creek report"
---

## Sites {#sec-sites}

```{r}
#| label: data
turbidity <- c(Upper = 4.2, Middle = 7.9, Lower = 12.6)
n_high <- sum(turbidity > 10)
```

We sampled three sites in 2024. One site read above the trigger of 10 NTU.

Then the author sets weft up:

weft::use_weft()
#> weft will set up creek-report:
#>   use_setup       .Rprofile (new), _weft.yml (new), report.qmd (edit)
#>   use_quarto      _extensions/weft-check/_extension.yml (new), _extensions/weft-check/weft-check.lua (new), _weft/pre-render.R (new), _weft/post-render.R (new), _quarto.yml (edit)
#>   use_dictionary  dict.yml (new), _weft/dict.schema.json (new)
#>   use_hooks       .git/hooks/commit-msg (new)
#>   use_ci          skipped: origin is not on GitHub
#>   use_agent_docs  AGENTS.md (new), .claude/skills/weft/SKILL.md (new)
#> Wrote: .Rprofile, _weft.yml, report.qmd, ...

vignette("setup", package = "weft") describes each of these files. The edit to report.qmd adds engine: knitr to its front matter.

git add .Rprofile _weft.yml report.qmd _extensions _weft _quarto.yml \
  dict.yml AGENTS.md .claude
git commit -m "Set up weft"
commit-msg: weft passed (1 changed file, 0.3 s)
[main 780cac8] Set up weft
 12 files changed, 1041 insertions(+)

The report still holds two typed numbers, “2024” and “10”. The gate lets them through, because it refuses only findings that HEAD did not hold. A project can adopt weft without fixing every old number first.

A new typed number

The author adds a sentence:

The highest reading was 12.6 NTU.
git add report.qmd
git commit -m "Report the highest reading"
commit-msg: 1 finding added that HEAD did not hold
  report.qmd
       15  numeral  "12.6" is a number typed in prose (rule 5.2.1).
                    Write it as a value, put it in the dictionary, or mark it [12.6]{.weft-literal why="..."}.

commit-msg: 0.3 s

The commit is refused. The hint lists the three fixes. Here the number is computed from data, so the author computes it. The trigger is a choice, so it goes in dict.yml:

trigger:
  value: 10
  type: quantity
  unit: NTU
  definition: "Turbidity above which a site is reported."

and the report becomes:

---
title: "Creek report"
engine: knitr
---

## Sites {#sec-sites}

```{r}
#| label: data
turbidity <- u(c(Upper = 4.2, Middle = 7.9, Lower = 12.6), NTU)
n_high <- sum(turbidity > dict$trigger)
```

We sampled three sites in 2024.
[No site | One site | # sites]{n="n_high"} read above the trigger of `r dict$trigger`{.num}.
The highest reading was `r claim(max(turbidity), . < u(50, NTU))`{.num}.
$ git add report.qmd dict.yml
$ git commit -m "Compute the highest reading"
commit-msg: weft passed (1 changed file, 0.3 s)
[main db9c980] Compute the highest reading

“2024” is still there and still tolerated. lints() lists every finding, old and new, if you want to see what remains (see vignette("lints", package = "weft")).

The ledger

Each render of a set-up project writes a ledger for each document: a record of every value and every chosen arm the render printed, with the sentence it sat in. It lives in _weft/ledger/, one folder per source:

_weft/ledger/report.qmd/report.jsonl
_weft/ledger/report.qmd/report.conditions.jsonl

Commit it with the source. Then git holds what each version of the report said, and changes() can compare them.

quarto render report.qmd
git add _weft/ledger
git commit -m "Render the report"

The ledger is JSON Lines. The first line records what the render read: the dictionary entries, the source files and any targets, each with a hash. Each later line is one entry:

{"weft":"ledger","version":1,"source":"report.qmd","output":"report","dict":{"trigger":"8e71a4f3e615896d"},"files":{"report.qmd":"7f971c44b8bcdfd7"},"targets":{}}
{"file":"report.qmd","section":"sec-sites","kind":"n","expr":"n_high","occ":1,"id":null,"context":"prose","text":"No site","arm":"zero","rel":"=","raw":0,"unit":null,"failed":null,"dict":[],"sentence":"No site read above the trigger of 10 NTU."}
{"file":"report.qmd","section":"sec-sites","kind":"value","expr":"dict$trigger","occ":1,"id":null,"context":"prose","text":"10 NTU","arm":null,"rel":"=","raw":10,"unit":"NTU","failed":null,"dict":["dict$trigger"],"sentence":"No site read above the trigger of 10 NTU."}

An entry is keyed by its file, its section anchor and its expression. That is why the lints ask for a {#id} on each heading: the key stays the same when the heading’s words change.

The condition log, report.conditions.jsonl, records each warning and error that a chunk or an inline expression raised during the render, and, for a document that reads targets, the ones recorded in the targets store. A new warning then shows in the diff, even when the output looks the same.

What changed: changes()

New data arrive. The Lower reading was 9.6, not 12.6, and the author adds a nitrate column whose values came from a laboratory as text:

turbidity <- u(c(Upper = 4.2, Middle = 7.9, Lower = 9.6), NTU)
n_high <- sum(turbidity > dict$trigger)
nitrate <- as.numeric(c("0.8", "<0.5", "1.1"))

After a render, changes() compares the ledgers in the working tree with those in HEAD:

weft::changes()
#> weft changes since HEAD (9e34dd7): 1 ledger compared; 2 changed, 0 added, 0 removed; 1 new condition
#>
#> Structural changes
#>   ~ report.qmd#sec-sites  n  n_high  [arm one -> zero, crosses 0]
#>       before: One site read above the trigger of 10 NTU.
#>       after:  No site read above the trigger of 10 NTU.
#>
#> Other changes, ranked
#>   ~ report.qmd#sec-sites  value  claim(max(turbidity), . < u(50, NTU))  [claim word "highest"]
#>       before: The highest reading was 12.6 NTU.
#>       after:  The highest reading was 9.6 NTU.
#>
#> New conditions
#>   ! report.qmd  chunk data  warning: NAs introduced by coercion

Read it from the top:

  • Structural changes come first. An arm changed, a value changed sign, crossed 0, 1 or a dictionary value, or moved by an order of magnitude. These are the changes most likely to make a sentence elsewhere wrong.
  • Other changes, ranked follow. A change beside a claim word, such as “highest” or “all”, ranks above a plain change; then larger relative changes rank higher.
  • New conditions lists warnings and errors the last committed render did not raise. Here as.numeric() turned “<0.5” into NA, which the output alone would not show.
  • Not re-rendered, when present, lists ledgers whose inputs (a dictionary entry, a source file, a target) changed after the render. Their values are stale.

A different value with the same printed text is not a change. changes() also lists tier-2 lint findings on lines added since the commit.

changes(since = ) compares with any commit, and print(x, brief = TRUE) prints only the header, the structural changes, the stale ledgers and the new conditions:

print(weft::changes(since = "9e34dd7"), brief = TRUE)
#> weft changes since 9e34dd7 (9e34dd7): 1 ledger compared; 1 changed, 0 added, 1 removed; 1 new condition
#>
#> Structural changes
#>   ~ report.qmd#sec-sites  n  n_high  [arm one -> zero, crosses 0]
#>       before: One site read above the trigger of 10 NTU.
#>       after:  No site read above the trigger of 10 NTU.
#>
#> New conditions
#>   ! report.qmd  chunk data  warning: NAs introduced by coercion

changes() renders nothing and writes nothing.

Removing constructs

A computed value, a span or a claim is a check. Deleting one is sometimes right, but it should never happen by accident. The author drops the sentence on the highest reading:

$ git commit -m "Drop the sentence on the highest reading"
commit-msg: 2 weft constructs removed, and the message does not say so

  report.qmd, as in HEAD
       17  claim(max(turbidity), . < u(50, NTU))
       17  `r claim(max(turbidity), . < u(50, NTU))`{.num}

  If the removal is intended, add this line at the end of the commit
  message, after a blank line:

      Weft-Removed: 2

  or commit with: git commit --trailer "Weft-Removed: 2"

commit-msg: 0.2 s

The value and its claim count as two constructs. The removal is intended, so the author says so:

$ git commit -m "Drop the sentence on the highest reading" --trailer "Weft-Removed: 2"
commit-msg: weft passed (1 changed file, 0.2 s)
[main c2ba829] Drop the sentence on the highest reading

The trailer stays in the history, so a reviewer can find every commit that removed checks with git log --grep "Weft-Removed". The number must match: a trailer that says 1 when 2 were removed is refused.

Construct errors

A construct error is refused in any changed file, even one that held it before:

$ git commit -m "Say which way turbidity moved"
commit-msg: 1 construct error
  report.qmd
       17  construct  A formatter on an `if` span is an error (rule 1.5.7): .num.

commit-msg: 0.2 s

Running the gate by hand

gate() is the function the hook runs. Call it to judge what is staged without committing:

weft::gate()
#> commit-msg: 1 finding added that HEAD did not hold
#>   report.qmd
#>        17  numeral  "3.4" is a number typed in prose (rule 5.2.1).
#>                     Write it as a value, put it in the dictionary, or mark it [3.4]{.weft-literal why="..."}.
#>
#> commit-msg: 0.3 s

It returns, invisibly, a list with ok and the findings, so a script can test weft::gate()$ok. gate(message = ) takes the path of a file holding a commit message, to check a Weft-Removed trailer. It judges the whole repository, including every subfolder that holds a _weft.yml.

The hook

use_hooks() writes .git/hooks/commit-msg. The script is POSIX sh and starts:

#!/bin/sh
# weft-file: use_hooks 0.0.0.9001 063f9359c3c3c3c91daa6def625f32d8
# The weft commit gate (rules 6.1 to 6.3), written by weft::use_hooks().
# Remove it with weft::use_hooks(remove = TRUE). Skip it for one commit
# with: git commit --no-verify

It records the Rscript and the library paths of the R session that ran use_hooks(), and runs R without the project’s .Rprofile or .Renviron. If you upgrade R or move your library, run use_hooks() again; status() reports a hook whose Rscript has gone.

When the repository already has a commit-msg hook from another tool, or uses a hook manager (core.hooksPath), use_hooks() leaves it alone, writes its script to .git/weft/commit-msg, and prints the line to add to the hook you already run.

git commit --no-verify skips every hook for one commit. It is there for emergencies, such as R being broken. It is not a way past a finding: answer the finding instead. use_hooks(remove = TRUE) removes the hook.

Before release: verify()

verify() is the full check. It has four parts:

Part What it does
lints runs the tier-1 lints over the whole project and compares them with a commit
decisions checks the decision pointers in dict.yml
render renders every document with Quarto (or knits it, under R Markdown), backing up and restoring _freeze, and reads the record each render leaves to see that every check ran and passed
ledger checks that no ledger is stale 
weft::verify()
#> weft verify: passed
#>   lints      1 tolerated finding
#>   decisions  0 pointers
#>   render     1 document rendered
#>   ledger     1 ledger checked
#>
#> Tolerated findings (rule 8.1.2); make a rule strict in _weft.yml when its count is 0:
#>   numeral         1 remain
#> weft verify: 4.7 s

The tolerated finding is the “2024” committed before weft. The count is a measure of how far adoption has come. When a rule’s count reaches 0, add it to strict in _weft.yml, and verify() then fails on any instance at all.

A render re-writes the ledgers. Commit them after verify() if they changed.

When something is wrong, verify() says what and fails. Here the Lower reading was mistyped as 79:

weft::verify()
#> weft verify: failed
#>   lints      1 tolerated finding
#>   decisions  0 pointers
#>   render     quarto exited with status 1; 1 failure, 0 not executed
#>   ledger     1 ledger checked
#>
#> Knit-time failures
#>   report.qmd
#>        17  failed claim  . < u(50, NTU) was FALSE (value 79 [NTU])
#>                          `r claim(max(turbidity), . < u(50, NTU))`
#>
#> Tier-2 findings on added lines
#>   report.qmd
#>        17  claim-word  Claim word "highest" in a sentence with a value; check that the value still bears it out, or guard the word with an `if` span (rule 5.5.1).
#>
#> Tolerated findings (rule 8.1.2); make a rule strict in _weft.yml when its count is 0:
#>   numeral         1 remain
#> weft verify: 4.9 s
#> Error: verify() failed: 2 reason(s); the report is above (rule 8.1.1).

A failing verify() signals an error of class weft_verify_error, so Rscript -e "weft::verify()" exits with status 1. Tier-2 findings are listed for a reader and never fail it.

Arguments narrow it:

  • verify(static = TRUE) runs the lints and the decision check only, with no render. It takes a second, and needs no data.
  • verify(files = "report.qmd") renders and judges some documents only.
  • verify(since = "v1.0") compares the lints with another commit.
weft::verify(static = TRUE)
#> weft verify: passed
#>   lints      1 tolerated finding
#>   decisions  0 pointers
#>   render     skipped: static = TRUE
#>   ledger     skipped: static = TRUE
#>
#> Tolerated findings (rule 8.1.2); make a rule strict in _weft.yml when its count is 0:
#>   numeral         1 remain
#> weft verify: 0.3 s

verify_skip in _weft.yml names parts to skip every time, for example verify_skip: [render] for a project whose data are not on every machine. status() reports a skipped part as off.

On pull requests: use_ci()

use_ci() writes .github/workflows/weft.yml, a GitHub Actions workflow that runs weft::verify(static = TRUE) on each pull request, compared with the branch it will merge into. It needs no data and no Quarto, so it runs for any project. use_weft() skips it unless origin is on GitHub.

The workflow catches a commit made with --no-verify, or on a machine without the hook.

Draft mode

While a chapter is half written, a failing claim or an unfinished span can get in the way. draft: true in _weft.yml (or the environment variable WEFT_DRAFT=1) makes a render report its failures and finish, with a marker such as <<weft: failed claim, line 20>> in the output in place of the value. See vignette("wording", package = "weft").

Draft mode does not change the commit gate, which still runs. verify() refuses to run in draft mode, because a draft render fails nothing:

weft::verify()
#> Error: verify() does not run in draft mode (rule 8.1.5): draft is on in _weft.yml. A draft render fails nothing, so it can verify nothing.

Turn draft mode off before release. status() shows it as off while it is on.

Seeing the set-up: status()

status() reports what weft has installed, and what is missing or out of date:

weft::status()
#> weft status: creek-report
#>   setup        ok        _weft.yml records weft 0.0.0.9001 (installed: 0.0.0.9001)
#>   activation   ok        route found (the .Rprofile)
#>   quarto       ok        extension, scripts and _quarto.yml entries are in place
#>   dictionary   ok        dict.yml and its schema are in place
#>   hooks        ok        the commit-msg hook is weft 0.0.0.9001, Rscript /usr/local/bin/Rscript
#>   ci           n/a       origin is not on GitHub
#>   agent docs   ok        the AGENTS.md block and the skill are current
#>   draft        ok        draft mode is off
#>   verify_skip  ok        verify() skips nothing
#>   strict       ok        no rule is strict
#> Nothing to install. Run weft::verify() to check the project.

It writes nothing and starts no R process.

A routine

  1. Write. Render as often as you like.
  2. Before each commit, read changes(). Look at every structural change and every new condition.
  3. Commit the source and the ledger together. Answer the gate if it refuses: compute the number, fix the construct, or add the trailer.
  4. Before you hand the report on, turn draft mode off and run verify().
